rules.statement: `mpn` is the orderable the datasheet prints, copied exactly with its suffix, not a package-only form that appears on no page.
`name` is the primary function as printed with the ASCII hyphen; extra functions of the same pad go in `alt_names`; a description is not an alternate function, so an exposed pad gets no `alt_names`.
An `alt_names` entry is another function of the same pad on the requested part; a sibling part's name in a shared cell, or a name from another package's pinout, is not an `alt_names` entry.

`group` is required for every pin of every repeated identical functional block, keyed by the datasheet's own label for the unit; both pins of one unit share one key; single-instance pins stay ungrouped.

`"power"` marks supplies in addition to a unit group, never instead of it; a supply block the datasheet prints on its own is grouped `power`; a lone supply may stay ungrouped; a node merely shared by every unit is not thereby a supply.

rules.statement: `electrical_type` follows the datasheet-says table: a supply or ground pin is `power_in` even when the I/O column says I, an open-drain output is `open_collector`, a three-state output is `tri_state`, an ADC input channel is `input`, and a pin with no signal direction is `passive`.
`extracted` means read from the datasheet; `inferred` covers every derived type, an interpreted dimension and an exposed-pad number the datasheet does not print; when unsure choose `inferred`.
`confirmed` is reserved for humans.
Every pin and every dimension cites a datasheet page >= 1 and a non-empty verbatim quote.
`pin_count` counts leads and pads but not the exposed pad; `pins` holds pin_count entries, plus one when `exposed_pad` is true.
Pin numbers are unique.
`electrical_type` is one of KiCad's pin types.
Each dimension carries at least one of min/nom/max, satisfies min <= nom <= max, and is positive except a min of 0.
`status` is extracted, inferred or confirmed; an inferred value is a warning for a human, not a failure.
A pin `number` is a string (`"1"`, `"A1"`).
A quote matches when it appears on the cited page with whitespace and line breaks collapsed.
A quote that appears only on another page is reported, not accepted.
An altered quote is reported, not silently accepted.
A cited page outside the PDF is reported.
Dimension sources are quote-checked exactly like pins.
A dimension gets min and max for a printed range, nom for TYP/BSC/one land-pattern number, max only for a MAX value, and all three for X +/- t.
Dimension names come from the defined name table; the ones the datasheet does not give are skipped.
standoff, lead_thickness and lead_length are named by the planes their extension lines span; a boxed BASIC or GAGE PLANE value is never one of them.
A parenthesised reference value never becomes a package dimension; it may be used for a land_* value, and a boxed BASIC value belongs to the land pattern.

Vendor letter tables map to the canonical names (A=height, A1=standoff, A2=body_thickness, b=lead_width, c=lead_thickness, D=body_length, e=pitch, body E=body_width, HE/E=overall_width, Lp/L=lead_length); the body-face-to-tip length (L, L1) is not lead_length.

land_* dimensions are the metal (the pad outline, the plain pad callouts, or the rectangle the note calls METAL COVERED BY SOLDER MASK), never the SOLDER MASK OPENING; land_pad_length, land_pad_width and land_span are recorded together or not at all.

A gold spec builds a symbol and, when the land pattern is complete, a footprint, and both load in kicad-cli; an incomplete land pattern skips the footprint with a warning naming the missing dimensions.
